lessons: Split scene keys at the last underscore. Instance suffixes are not persistent identities.
Use normalized basket orientation and dimensions for containment and release-site margins.
Scene heights are nominal category planes. Height changes, disappearance, and unchanged suffixes cannot verify a grasp.
The supplied manual offset intervention improved some development delivery proxies, but did not establish general feasibility or full success.
Test offset release endpoints at their intended release altitude before closing a gripper. Basket centers and higher clearance endpoints can be unreachable.
Prefer the destination-side arm for lateral baskets; use bounded alternate-arm checks only before contact.
Complete one category before scattering effort across categories. Open both grippers initially and release explicitly after each transfer.
Only an explicit no_collision_free_path response certifies zero execution. Other errors stop execution without speculative recovery.
Following a rejected transport, a controlled return to the original contact support is preferable to opening at an arbitrary location.
Reservations record commanded release sites, not verified deliveries. Returning from policy does not establish task completion.
The public interface provides neither home motion nor guaranteed initial Cartesian poses. Do not fabricate a home command or claim that retreat restores the initial poses.

rationale: This proposal addresses the recorded transport failures by physically checking bounded, geometry-constrained offset destinations before grasping, at the intended release altitude rather than an assumed feasible high basket waypoint. It favors destination-side arms, preserves existing groupings through bounded assignment, and prioritizes finishing categories. Both grippers start open; successful release sequences include an open-gripper retreat. Explicit zero-execution transport rejection permits controlled source-site rollback, while uncertain execution stops without speculative manipulation. RPC accounting reserves capacity for recovery. No home API or initial Cartesian pose is invented, and neither perception nor program return is treated as native success.
